headline: The US Army is creating a new command and a new buying office to speed up its use of machines that can act with little human control.
score_reason: Pool score kept: official Army memo and statement, large reorganisation; no sign the headline is overstated.
importance_line: The Army is reorganising to buy and field more autonomous weapons and vehicles, which affects soldiers who will fight alongside them and the companies that sell to the Army; the reporting rests on one memo, and no budget or full timeline is given beyond a 2028 target.
summary: Breaking Defense reports, citing a memo it reviewed that was signed by Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle and a statement from an Army spokesperson, that the Army will set up a Futures and Autonomous Systems Command and a new executive office for buying autonomous systems; Axios reported it first. The memo tells that office to prioritize getting autonomous weapons, combat vehicles and supply boats into service no later than the 2028 budget year, and to expand two specialist jobs, drone technicians and robotics technicians, to all applicable Army units.
notes: Original outlet Axios (blocked, HTTP 403); written from Breaking Defense. Memo dated 1 Oct 2026, first reported 2 Oct 2026. Builds on Hegseth’s AUTOWARCOM announcement of 30 Sep 2026.
